edition.title: Slow Burn - Tuesday 27 October 2026
edition.fact: Edition 22. Anthropic picks a ticker, Jio picks a price. Tuesday 27 October 2026, edition 22. Anthropic files publicly for a Nasdaq listing under the ticker ANT - $16.3 billion of first-half revenue against a record $80.7 billion accounting-charge loss; Jio Platforms <Fix>fixed its issue price at Rs 1,119 on Saturday</Fix> and lists tomorrow; the Sensex rebounds 483 points as Infosys swallows its guidance cut whole; Ather Energy posts its first profitable quarter and hits the circuit; and the Fed decides tomorrow with a hold priced in and December in play.
edition.intro: The 5-minute lead route is first; sections carry the detail. This is the eve of a double Wednesday: the Fed's rate call and the largest listing in Indian market history land within hours of each other. The long read is the Anthropic story - the lab that walked out of OpenAI, said no to the Pentagon, and just asked the public market for a verdict.

blocks.html: Anthropic files for its IPO: the five-year-old maker of Claude plans to list on the Nasdaq as "ANT"; the S-1 shows revenue going from $41 million in 2023 to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026, and a record $80.7 billion loss that is mostly an accounting charge. Detail.
Jio Platforms lists tomorrow: issue price fixed at Rs 1,119, the Rs 30,188-crore IPO subscribed 22.2 times, valuation about Rs 10.3 lakh crore. Detail.
The rebound: Sensex +482.92 to 73,606.75, Nifty +0.68% to 22,753.20, closing at the day's high; Infosys gapped down 4% on its guidance cut and closed at its day high, up 0.9%. Detail.
Ather's first profit: Rs 1.26 crore against a Rs 154 crore loss a year ago; the stock hit its circuit and closed +13.7%. Detail.
Fed eve: a hold at 4.00% is expected tomorrow; futures price an 84-87% chance of a December hike. Monthly expiry today. Detail.
The swing desk, one week in: three watchlist triggers hit on Monday, one judgment call proven right, and the single live setup still waiting for its price. Detail.
The long read: Anthropic - the company that said no. Named people, dated scenes, and what would prove the story wrong. Detail.

1. Anthropic asks the public market for a verdict. The company behind Claude filed its S-1 - the registration document a company must publish before listing in the US - with the SEC on Monday, planning a Nasdaq listing under the ticker "ANT" (CNBC's live coverage). The numbers in it: revenue of $41 million in 2023, $4.6 billion in 2025, and $16.3 billion in the first six months of 2026 alone; a net loss of $80.7 billion for that half, a record for any IPO filer, which the company attributes mostly to accounting charges rather than cash burn (Fortune's read of the filing; the 2025 loss was $42 billion on the same basis). The debut is targeted for Thanksgiving week, which would put Anthropic on the public market before OpenAI, the company its founders left. Why it matters to you: this is the first public balance sheet of the AI boom - every private valuation in your AI Race section now has a comparable with audited numbers attached. Editor's takeaway: the loss figure will dominate headlines; the revenue line is the one that decides the price.

2. Jio Platforms: Rs 1,119, tomorrow. Reliance Industries' digital arm fixed its issue price at Rs 1,119 a share on Saturday - the top of the Rs 1,065-1,119 band - after the Rs 30,188-crore offer was subscribed 22.2 times, valuing Jio at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore going into Wednesday's listing (moneycontrol). This edition's earlier coverage tracked the demand build day by day; the final print reconciles with the exchange's consolidated schedule. Why it matters to you: the largest listing in Indian market history lands on the same morning as the Fed decision - two liquidity events, one day, and the day's breadth will show whether domestic money can absorb both. Editor's takeaway: a 22-times book prices perfection into day one; what matters for the index is where the stock settles by Friday, not where it opens.

3. The bounce that held to the bell. Monday snapped the four-session losing streak: the Sensex rose 482.92 points (0.66%) to 73,606.75 and the Nifty 153.20 points (0.68%) to 22,753.20 - closing at the day's exact high, with IT and metals leading (TOI; India Today; NSE index data). The day's real test was Infosys: it opened 3.1% down on Friday night's FY27 guidance cut, fell as much as 3.9%, and then rallied to close at its day's high of Rs 1,165.00 - up 0.9% on the day (BSE official data). Foreign investors sold Rs 1,462.49 crore while domestic institutions bought Rs 2,609.57 crore (provisional exchange data via Hindu BusinessLine's wrap). Why it matters to you: a guidance cut absorbed in a single session is how strong tapes behave - the swing desk's Infosys call, judged by its own published rule, was absorption. Editor's takeaway: one good day after four bad ones is a bounce, not a trend; the Fed decides which it was.

4. Ather Energy's first profitable quarter. The electric two-wheeler maker reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 1.26 crore for the September quarter - against a Rs 154.07 crore loss a year ago - on total income up 62% year on year, with EBITDA margin improving about 1,450 basis points to 4.9% (company's exchange-filed press release). The board approved Rs 122 crore of capex to expand the Hosur and AURIC plants. The stock hit its 10% upper circuit intraday and closed up 13.7% at Rs 1,574.00 (BSE official data). Why it matters to you: the first listed EV maker to cross into profit changes the question for the whole sector from "when do losses end" to "what is the profit worth". Editor's takeaway: Rs 1.26 crore is a rounding error as profit and a milestone as direction - the market priced the direction.

5. The Fed holds its breath, and your insurance desk watches IRDAI's pile. Tomorrow's FOMC decision: futures price roughly a 9-10% chance of a hike this week and an 84-87% chance of one by December, with the policy rate expected to stay at 4.00% (Investing.com's pre-meeting read). Three of the seven mega-cap US tech names report this week. In India, the monthly derivatives expiry lands today. Separately, and closer to your desk: IRDAI - the insurance regulator - is working through more than 650 stakeholder submissions on its proposed overhaul of insurance distribution (moneycontrol, 26 Oct); what emerges will redraw how policies are sold and who gets paid for selling them. Why it matters to you: the distribution review is the biggest structural rewrite your industry has had in years, and its drafting stage is now. Editor's takeaway: a hold is priced as certain, so the statement's December language is the trade, not the decision.

Monday, the full picture. The Nifty's day: open 22,524.40, low 22,387.35, close 22,753.20 - at the day's high, up 0.68% (NSE index data; wraps per TOI and India Today). The Sensex closed at 73,606.75 (+482.92). Bank Nifty added 79.33 points to 54,367; the midcap index gained 665 points to 56,465. Breadth and leadership: IT and metals led the rebound (India Today), with Infosys, JSW Steel (+5.94%) and Dr Reddy's (+6.41%) among the index heavyweights carrying the day (BSE official data). Flows were two-sided again: FII selling of Rs 1,462.49 crore met DII buying of Rs 2,609.57 crore (provisional exchange data). Brent eased to about $114-115 (5paisa's post-close print: $114.25), giving the market one less headwind than Friday's $116.72 settle.

blocks.html: What Tuesday watches. The monthly derivatives expiry lands today, on the eve of the Fed; options desks typically keep positions light into both. Results continue - over 450 companies report this week, with Maruti Suzuki, L&T, Vedanta, Coal India and NTPC among the larger names on the calendar (ET Now's results calendar). And the setup for Wednesday is now double: the FOMC statement and Jio's first trade. Framed as what to watch, never what to buy.

Jio Platforms, the eve of listing. Price fixed on Saturday at Rs 1,119 (exchange-filed Reliance letter, 24 Oct); 22.2 times subscribed across categories; Rs 30,188 crore raised; pre-listing valuation about Rs 10.3 lakh crore (moneycontrol). The anchor book - a third of the institutional portion, locked in before the public offer - drew bids from global funds at the same price. What to watch tomorrow: the open matters less than the close, and the close matters less than where the stock settles by Friday, when the flippers are done. Editor's takeaway: India's largest listing is also a liquidity test for every other large cap - watch whether the index can hold 22,700 while money rotates into Jio.

Tonbo Imaging, one week on. The defence-optics maker that this paper covered as a case study listed at a 66% premium on 23 October after a 135.9-times subscription (Zee Business, ET). Context for Jio's day: Tonbo shows what retail enthusiasm does to a small float; Jio is the opposite test - the country's biggest float finding a price with everyone already inside.

blocks.html: Gainers, with the why. Ather Energy (+13.74%): first profitable quarter - details on the front page. MRPL, the Mangalore refiner (+12.66%): no exchange-filed catalyst; the move tracked a Choice Institutional Equities note and refining-margin interest (Business Today) - labelled a brokerage-driven move, not company news. Apollo Micro Systems (+9.99%): record Q2 revenue, EBITDA and profit, with the order book at a record high (Business Standard). Dr Reddy's (+6.41%): no confirmed catalyst; the day's wraps list pharma among the supporting sectors. JSW Steel (+5.94%): metals led the day; see the swing desk for what it did to a published trigger.

Losers, with the why. The day's real story was a cluster: AU Small Finance Bank (-6.91%), City Union Bank (-6.09%), Five-Star Business Finance (-7.45%), Ujjivan Small Finance (-4.09%) and Shriram Finance (-5.02%) all fell together (moves on BSE closes; NSE prints differ slightly) - lenders sold despite strong profit growth. AU SFB's own print was PAT up 53% to Rs 858 crore with deposits up 29% and loans up 25% (company press release); the selloff flagged margin pressure and higher slippages - the portion of loans going bad - with brokerages split on valuation (Hindu BusinessLine, Business Today). Sky Gold (-10.47%): no confirmed catalyst. The why behind the cluster: when funding costs rise and unsecured lending slows, the market sells the lender's future margins before they show up in the books - the guidance language, not the quarter, sets the price.

REC declared a second interim dividend of Rs 3.50 a share alongside Monday's results (profit fell 21% year on year; NDTV Profit). Tech Mahindra's Rs 15 interim dividend is in payment (record date 23 October, payment by 13 November); the record date for its proposed 1:1 bonus is still unannounced - shareholder approval by postal ballot is in progress, and the company has said the date "will be intimated separately". Ather Energy's board approved Rs 122 crore of capacity capex (company filing).

1. IRDAI's distribution overhaul: 650-plus submissions and counting. The insurance regulator is reconciling more than 650 stakeholder responses to its proposed redrawing of insurance distribution - who may sell policies, how agents and brokers are paid, and what insurers must disclose (moneycontrol, 26 Oct). The mechanism: distribution cost is built into every premium, so the rewrite touches pricing, commissions and the agency model at once. For someone inside the industry, the consultation draft is the document to read before the final norms land - the submissions window is where the shape gets set. Editor's takeaway: the last distribution rewrite took years to bite; this one's 650 responses mean every lobby is already at the table.

2. The lender selloff is a margin story, not a results story. Monday's cluster fall in small finance banks and NBFCs (Top movers) came on prints that showed 25-53% profit growth. The mechanism: markets price the next four quarters, not the last one - when management flags funding-cost pressure and rising slippages (AU SFB's commentary; broker notes per Business Today), the multiple compresses before the margin does. What to watch: Q3 commentary on unsecured-lending slippages across the sector. Editor's takeaway: in lender stocks, the guidance sentence costs more than the quarter earns.

3. Oil's refund, and what stays priced. Brent at about $114.25 after the Indian close (5paisa) is roughly $2.5 below Friday's settle - the market refunding a slice of the Iran premium. Every dollar on crude adds about $2 billion a year to India's import bill (this paper's standing math, from the petroleum ministry's import volumes), so Friday-to-Monday is worth about $5 billion of annualized bill either way. What to watch: whether $112-113 - the pre-escalation shelf - holds as support into Wednesday's Fed. Editor's takeaway: the premium leaks on words and refills on strikes; until a signed deal, trade the range, not the direction - as analysis of pricing, not advice.

The funding cooldown, in numbers. Indian startups raised $96 million across 15 deals in the third week of October (YourStory's weekly tracker) - the second straight week under $100 million, with deeptech the only pocket drawing global cheques. Against that, the year's two biggest liquidity events are both this quarter: Jio lists tomorrow and Anthropic filed Monday. The insight of the day: private markets are rationing seed-to-Series-B capital while public markets pay record prices for scale - the gap between "fundable story" and "listable business" has rarely been wider, and founders are being sorted accordingly.

Opportunity watch. Nothing verified this cycle clears the bar for a specific grant, programme or competition deadline worth your time this week; the honest entry is an empty slot rather than a padded one.

Startup idea (one, as specified). A compliance-tracker for insurance distribution: 650-plus submissions into IRDAI mean the final norms will differ from the draft in ways every insurer, broker and agent must map to their own contracts and payouts. A product that ingests the final notification, diffs it against the draft, and produces a per-firm change list - what your commission terms, disclosures and licensing must say by the effective date - sells to exactly the people filing those 650 responses. The wedge is timing: norms land once, and the first credible mapping tool owns the renewal cycle.

1. Inside Anthropic's S-1, the first public AI balance sheet. The filing (Monday; CNBC's live coverage) puts Anthropic on the Nasdaq as "ANT", targeted for Thanksgiving week. Revenue: $41 million (2023), $4.6 billion (2025), $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 - growth driven this year by Claude Code, its programming agent, and the Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models (June 2026). The $80.7 billion first-half net loss is mostly accounting charges - non-cash entries tied to how the company must revalue its funding instruments - with the 2025 loss at $42 billion on the same basis (Fortune's read of the filing). The last private round: $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation in May 2026, co-led by Altimeter, then the largest private valuation in AI - above OpenAI's (Reuters; TechCrunch). The filing also lands mid-dispute with the US government - the full story is today's long read. Editor's takeaway: read the revenue slope and ignore the loss headline - the slope is what public investors are actually being asked to price.

2. OpenAI answered on the same day: GPT-6.1 Terra. OpenAI released GPT-6.1 Terra on Monday (OpenAI's announcement and developer docs): a fast, efficient model built for detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use - operating a screen, clicking and typing - at scale. Vendor claims, labelled; independent evaluations do not exist yet. The verified facts: the model exists, its stated purpose is computer use, and its release on Anthropic's filing day was not a coincidence worth ignoring. Editor's takeaway: the frontier fight has moved from chat quality to who operates the computer - watch where the agent benchmarks, not the chat ones, move this quarter.

3. Radar. Nothing else in the last 48 hours cleared the verification bar for the radar; OpenAI's release notes also updated Monday (OpenAI) with no separately material item found. An empty radar line is a result, not a gap.

Claude Code's presence in an IPO filing is the tell for your own stack: Anthropic's 2026 growth is attributed, in the company's own framing, to a coding agent selling to enterprises - meaning agentic coding is now a revenue line on a public balance sheet, not a demo. Practically, this week: GPT-6.1 Terra's computer-use pitch and Claude Code's filing-grade traction point at the same build pattern - agents that operate tools, not just write text. If you are building with either, the durable skill is writing the harness: the permissions, the test loop, and the rollback, because the model layer is now swapping every few weeks while the harness is what keeps your product standing. Treat both vendors' capability claims as brochures until your own test suite confirms them on your workload.

Read an IPO filing's risk factors like an analyst (about 20 minutes). Anthropic's S-1 is public on the SEC's EDGAR database (sec.gov, search "Anthropic"). Skip the business description and go straight to "Risk Factors" - the section companies must write against themselves. Your exercise: pull out three risks in your own words, and require that one of them is not about money - a governance, dependence or regulatory risk. Then compare your three against what the coverage emphasized. A good result: you find at least one risk the headlines ignored (hint: check what the filing says about its two largest backers also being its competitors). Time: 20 minutes. The skill transfers to every Indian IPO you read - the DRHP's risk section is the same animal.

groups.heading: One concept: the $80.7 billion paper loss

blocks.html: Anthropic lost $80.7 billion in six months and is also one of the fastest-growing companies ever measured. Both are true, and the mechanism is fair-value accounting. When a startup raises money by selling preferred shares or convertible instruments, accounting rules can require the company to revalue those instruments on its own books as its valuation rises. Anthropic's private value went from a few billion dollars in 2023 to $965 billion in May 2026; each step up forces a larger non-cash charge through the profit-and-loss statement - the company's own success, booked as a loss. No cash leaves the building; the charge reflects what it would cost to repay those investors at today's price. At IPO, the instruments convert to ordinary shares and the charges stop - which is why pre-IPO losses of this kind inflate right up to listing day and then vanish. The decision rule: in any pre-IPO filing, find the operating line or the cash-burn line and read the net loss only after checking how much of it is this revaluation. Sixty-second recall, closed book: (1) What triggers the charge? (2) Does cash leave the company? (3) Why does it stop at IPO? Answers: a rising valuation on preferred/convertible instruments; no; conversion to ordinary shares ends the remeasurement.

The registration statement a company files with the US Securities and Exchange Commission before going public - business description, audited financials, risk factors, cap table and who is selling. Companies may first file confidentially (Anthropic did, in June 2026) to negotiate with the SEC out of public view; the public S-1 is the version investors price from. India's equivalent document is the DRHP - draft red herring prospectus - filed with SEBI.
Week one, scored. Monday's close on official BSE data, measured against the published levels (the rules and ledger File):

items.title: HCL Technologies - the one live setup: untriggered
items.detail: Monday low Rs 1,385.10 against the Rs 1,351-1,378 entry zone; closed Rs 1,418.00. No fill, no gain, no loss. Four sessions of validity remain (today through Friday 30 Oct), then it lapses.

items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank - trigger hit
items.detail: Held above Rs 437.55 all day (low Rs 437.80), closed Rs 441.00, +2.5%. A watchlist trigger is a graduation signal, not an entry - nothing was bought, so there is nothing to book.

items.title: JSW Steel - trigger hit
items.detail: Held the Rs 1,158.95 floor (low Rs 1,187.95) and closed at the day high of Rs 1,257.55, above the Rs 1,218.90-1,222.30 reclaim zone, +5.9%. It stays out of setups by design - its published risk-reward screen failed at 1:1.2.

items.title: ONGC - marginal
items.detail: Closed Rs 228.25, a quarter-rupee above the Rs 228 breakout mark; crude eased off Friday. A close that close to the line is a watch, not a verdict.

items.title: Infosys - judgment confirmed
items.detail: The published call was that absorption of the guidance cut keeps it on watch; Monday gapped down 3.1%, fell as much as 3.9%, and closed at the day high, up 0.9%. Absorbed.

items.title: Tech Mahindra - quiet
items.detail: High Rs 1,806.40 against the Rs 1,845.95 reclaim trigger; closed Rs 1,798.00. Bonus record date still unannounced.

blocks.html: So, is anything paying off? The honest answer after week one: the only actual setup has not triggered - HCLTech never came back to its zone, so there is no trade, no profit and no loss. The watchlist, which costs nothing and risks nothing, called the day: three of five names hit their published triggers and the fourth judgment (Infosys) was right. That is evidence about selection, not returns; the log books returns only when a setup actually fills. No new setup clears the bar today - Ather's circuit day leaves no honest entry structure at Rs 1,574, so it goes on watch for how the Rs 1,380-1,400 breakout area holds. Empty slots stay empty by design.

Wednesday is a double verdict on appetite: the Fed tells markets what money costs in December, and Jio tells India what scale is worth on listing day - while Anthropic's S-1 tells everyone what an AI leader actually earns. The thread connecting all three is the same question your swing desk answers every week: is there real demand under the story? Infosys's Monday - down 4%, closed at the high - says Indian IT's buyers are waiting at lower prices, not leaving. Confidence: moderate. What would change my mind: a weak Jio close on listing day with the index failing to hold 22,700, which would say the liquidity is rotation, not addition.

1. IRDAI's final distribution norms. 650-plus submissions are being reconciled now (Finance Goldmine). Watch for: the final notification and its effective date; what would prove the overhaul has teeth: commission and disclosure language that survives the lobbying intact.

2. Tech Mahindra's bonus record date. The postal ballot for the 1:1 bonus is in progress; the record date "will be intimated separately". Watch for: the exchange filing announcing it. What would shelve it: nothing on file suggests it - treat as pending, not at risk.

3. The December Fed. A hold tomorrow is priced at ~90%; a December hike at 84-87% (Investing.com). Watch for: the statement's inflation language and the press conference's December hints. What would prove the market wrong: a surprise hike tomorrow - low probability, high impact, and the reason expiry-day positions stay light.
